headline: Congress cancels a National Park Service rule that limited off-road vehicle use in parts of Glen Canyon National Recreation Area.
what_it_does: This law overturns a National Park Service rule published on January 13, 2025, that restricted off-road vehicles such as ATVs and off-highway vehicles in parts of Glen Canyon National Recreation Area in Arizona and Utah. The rule had banned these vehicles on an 8-mile stretch of the Poison Spring Loop in the Orange Cliffs Special Management Unit. It had also removed the Park Service's power to open the upper Flint Trail to off-road vehicles and limited off-road driving from certain roads to the Lake Powell shoreline. With the rule canceled, those limits do not apply.

who_it_affects.group: People who drive ATVs and other off-road vehicles in Glen Canyon
who_it_affects.how: They are no longer bound by the 2025 rule's limits on the Poison Spring Loop segment and on routes from certain roads to the Lake Powell shoreline.
The agency's 2025 off-road vehicle rule for Glen Canyon is void, and under the Congressional Review Act it generally cannot issue a substantially similar rule without new approval from Congress.

who_it_affects.group: Visitors to Lake Powell and the Orange Cliffs area
who_it_affects.how: Areas that the rule had closed to off-road vehicles may again see that kind of vehicle use.
